technologies.title: Open architecture, shown clearly.
technologies.description: Select any layer to see how OpenMeet moves a conversation from one browser to another.

vue.label: Vue browser
vue.title: Vue 3 + XState
vue.description: A fast, reactive interface keeps meeting state predictable while media stays in the browser.

signaling.label: Signaling
signaling.title: WebSocket + Axum
signaling.description: A lightweight signaling channel coordinates room entry, negotiation, and participant events.

sfu.label: Media router
sfu.title: Rust WebRTC SFU
sfu.description: A high-performance Rust SFU forwards each audio and video stream without mixing or recording it.

webrtc.label: Live delivery
webrtc.title: WebRTC
webrtc.description: Browsers receive adaptive real-time media with low latency and no application download.

turn.label: Connection fallback
turn.title: STUN + TURN
turn.description: When a direct network path is difficult, TURN provides a reliable route for meeting traffic.

postgres.label: Optional accounts
postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Account data is isolated from ephemeral room media. Guests never need an account to talk.

idea.title: Born from one simple question.
idea.question: What if starting a video call felt as open as starting a conversation?
idea.description: OpenMeet began in Zurich with the goal of making video conversations accessible directly from a browser. No application download. No registration wall. No login before hello. Privacy comes first, while technology stays out of the way.

freedom.imageAlt: People collaborating around their own computers
freedom.title: The freedom to speak without being profiled.
freedom.description: Safe conversation should not depend on being tracked, categorized, or locked into someone else's platform. Everyone should be able to talk privately and choose infrastructure they can inspect or own.
freedom.infrastructure: Privacy can live on infrastructure you control
